title: Unify client resilience patterns with TTL-bucketed backoff and SLO-aware failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Client libraries across services implement inconsistent retry/timeout/backoff behavior which causes unpredictable cross-region failover, duplicate side-effects, and oscillating load during partial outages. This ticket defines a single, implementable resilience pattern for SDKs and services that aligns with SLOs, supports multi-region failover, and integrates circuit breakers and load-shedding.

Goals: 1) Define a TTL-bucketed backoff algorithm that is deterministic and cacheable across retries (so hedged requests and client-side caches interact predictably). 2) Standardize idempotency key use and semantics for mutating operations across services. 3) Provide a client-side SLO-aware governor that can engage per-region circuit-breakers and perform fast failover with safe hedging semantics. 4) Produce an SDK spec and runtime checks, with instrumentation and QA plan for rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document approved by Platform Reliability and SDK leads
SDK reference implementation (Go + TypeScript) passes integration tests against a failure-injection harness
All services adopt idempotency key guidelines or document why they are incompatible
Heartbeat metrics and SLO telemetry for client-side failover are emitted and visible on Console dashboards
Rollout plan with canary gates and rollback triggers defined
implementation_plan: Draft spec: TTL-bucketed backoff with three buckets (fast jittered retries, steady exponential, long-steady retries) and clear boundaries for hedged fanout
Define idempotency contract: header name, TTL semantics, storage recommendations, and explicit error mappings on duplicate detection
Circuit-breaker policy: per-region sliding-window error rate + SLA-aware threshold, open cooldown, and progressive backoff for probe requests
SLO-aware load-shedding: client reads SLO signals (latency/error ratios) from runtime or Console endpoint and reduces concurrency or shifts traffic to fallback regions
Create Go and TS SDK implementations with feature flag gating and environment variable overrides
Build a failure injection harness (local + CI) that simulates partial region outages, tail latency spikes, and duplicated request delivery
Integration tests: idempotency propagation, hedged request correctness, no unbounded duplicate side effects, and metrics emission
metrics_and_observability: dashboard: Per-route token-level cost/latency with failover annotations
rollout_plan: Week 0: Spec review and sign-off with Reliability, SDK, and Product teams
Week 1: Merge SDK feature-flagged implementation behind rv_client_resilience flag
Week 2: Canary 5% of internal traffic (non-customer) and run failure-injection test suite hourly
Week 3: Expand to 25% and monitor circuit-breaker opens, idempotency_conflicts, and SLO delta; hold if regressions detected
Week 4: Gradual 100% rollout for internal services; enable opt-in for customer-facing SDKs with migration notes
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window followed by mandatory postmortem if SLO regressions > 0.5%

comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after cross-team workshop with Platform Reliability and SDK leads. Workshop consensus: single backoff primitive + idempotency standardization needed to avoid cascading retries during region flaps.

2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor: Prototype TTL-buckets implemented in go-client branch 'resilience/ttl-buckets'. Early findings: hedged requests reduce tail latency but can double upstream QPS if idempotency isn't enforced. Need mandatory idempotency headers for mutating calls.

2026-03-11 Mei Chen (Reliability): Proposed circuit-breaker heuristic uses 1m sliding window with both error rate and p99 latency thresholds. Suggested adding a 'probe' token budget to avoid total traffic blackhole after open state.

2026-03-12 Rory Singh (SDK): Reviewed TS SDK changes. Requested clearer API for passing idempotency keys and opt-out escape hatches for very low-level internal calls. Also requested sample migration guide for services that rely on eventual-consistency duplicates.

2026-03-13 Ops Alert: Simulated regional latency injection shows hedged fanout at 3x in naive clients. Action: add default hedged fanout limit of 2 and require explicit opt-in for >2. Added to implementation_plan.

2026-03-13 QA: Added tests to CI harness that assert no more than 1 duplicate side-effect for idempotent operations under 95th percentile of failure scenarios. Failing tests documented in GH issue linked above.
